title: Nurse NDE 6900
content: I was diagnosed with eclampsia. [Editor's note: An acute and life-threatening complication of pregnancy.] They gave me a C-section in the afternoon. In the evening, I was having trouble breathing; it felt like an elephant on my chest. I was on oxygen but I was watching my oxygen saturations decrease. I was terrified. Next, everything went pitch black. Then I felt a pop and I was out of my body. I was floating. I felt unbelievably good, about a million times better than I ever could imagine. When I looked down, I thought, 'I look terrible'. Next, I saw my urine collection bag and the urine was brown. I thought I am in liver failure. The bag was attached to the side of the bed near where my feet were. I felt myself saying, 'What about my baby?' I felt the answer, 'That she would have the people she needed when she needed them.' I am hearing plastic being opened and people yelling. I notice I am standing in the back of the room and my deceased Father is there. He had been dead about nine years then. He took me into his arms, we were dancing, and he was singing to me. He sang the same way he sang when I was a child. He told me it wasn't my time. I remember opening my eyes and looking at the ceiling. I was in horrible pain from head to toe. I was angry. I heard the doctor saying I had congestive heart failure (CHF). I pulled the oxygen off me. With labored breathing, I sat up and tried to yell, 'How did I get CHF from a Cesarean section?' I fell back onto the bed and someone put an oxygen mask on me. There were about ten people in the room. They started throwing all kinds of equipment on my bed and wheeling me to the Intensive Care Unit.

context.nde_cause_other_detail: Eclampsia with C-section; later breathing trouble and reported congestive heart failure (CHF).

stage_sequence.elements_other_detail: Initial pitch blackness before OBE; auditory perception of 'plastic being opened and people yelling'; concern about baby with reassuring answer.
stage_sequence.sequence_variation_description: Blackness → 'pop' and OBE floating → observations in hospital room → encounter with deceased father → told it wasn't her time → return to body with pain and distress.

unique_elements.nonstandard_elements: Observed urine collection bag with brown urine and inferred liver failure while out of body; received reassurance about baby ('she would have the people she needed when she needed them').
unique_elements.notable_quotes: “Next, everything went pitch black. Then I felt a pop and I was out of my body.”; “I felt unbelievably good, about a million times better than I ever could imagine.”; “What about my baby?” / “That she would have the people she needed when she needed them.”; “He told me it wasn't my time.”
